transcript.content: Hi, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, it's a little hard to explain without sounding, you know, unreasonable. But for almost two years now, ever since this one big commission I had, I've just had this... this certainty that a few people in the ensemble are sort of quietly undermining my work. 

I know that probably sounds a bit dramatic, and I really try to be easy to work with, but they do these things—like sudden schedule changes, or shifting seating choices, or making these little comments during rehearsals. And even when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain why they're doing it, I just... I can't shake the feeling that it's intentional. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting, but it's just been really bothering me.
When they show you clear evidence that there was an innocent reason for something, are you able to accept that explanation?

Well, I try to. I really, really try to just nod and say, 'Okay, that makes sense,' because I don't want to be difficult. I want to be a good director, you know? But... even when I see the emails, or they show me the notes... I just can't. It's like... I just know it's not the whole truth. 

I mean, I don't say that to them, of course! I'm always very polite about it. But inside, I just have this... this absolute certainty that those little comments and schedule changes are intentional, meant to undermine me. It's been like this for almost two years, ever since that big commission. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, like I'm just being paranoid or something. Do you think I'm being unreasonable? I just can't seem to let it go, no matter how hard I try to see their side of it.
Is there any part of you that thinks you might be mistaken about them undermining you?

I really, really want to say yes to that. I know the reasonable thing to do would be to admit that I could be wrong, and I'd love to be able to tell you that I have doubts. I want to be a flexible, easygoing director, I promise I do. 

But... honestly? Um... no. I just can't. Like I was saying, for almost two years now, ever since that commission, I just haven't been able to shake this absolute certainty about it. Even when they put those supposedly innocent emails or notes right in front of my face to explain away the schedule changes or the weird seating choices... I just know they're quietly undermining my work. 

I'm so sorry, I know repeating that probably makes me sound incredibly stubborn or... or difficult, doesn't it? I really don't want you to think I'm just being closed-minded. I just can't make myself believe their explanations, no matter how much I want to be agreeable about it.
Have you ever heard voices when no one was there?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely not. I've never experienced anything like that. I mean, I know sometimes people going through stressful things can, you know, have things like that happen, but... no. My hearing is perfectly fine, just the normal sounds around me. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm just dealing with this situation with the ensemble, nothing... nothing like hearing voices. That would be really concerning, right? I promise I'm just trying to figure out how to handle the work stuff.
Before this started two years ago, had you generally been a very mistrustful person?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always tried to be really open and trusting with people, especially in my field. You have to be, right? Music is so collaborative. I've always prided myself on being someone who gives others the benefit of the doubt and works well with a team. 

I mean, before all this started with the ensemble, I never had any issues like this. I had great relationships with my colleagues in grad school and on my early projects. I really hope I'm not coming across as some bitter, suspicious person now. I don't want to be that way. It's just... this specific situation, with this specific group of people, it's just so clear to me what they're doing. But generally speaking, no, I've always been very trusting. Is that... does that make sense? I hope it shows that I'm trying to be reasonable about all this.

latest_inference.note: F60.0 ruled out because the mistrust is not longstanding or pervasive; it began about two years ago in a circumscribed work context after previously being generally trusting. Persistent fixed persecutory belief without hallucinations supports F22.
